title: Degree-zero modules, bounds, and continuity
statement: For the standard derived categories of [lem-pe-coefficient-comparison-data], the degree-zero embedding is fully faithful, its objects are bounded in the sense of [lem-pe-coefficient-bounded-classical-descent], and its degree-zero cohomology is the original module. A module with invertible continuity maps as in [det-pe-classical-definition-continuity-map] has continuous cohomology after degree-zero embedding. Moreover a functor compatible with degree-zero embeddings is fully faithful if its derived functor induces bijections on morphisms between bounded objects.

proof.text:
degree zero cohomology is naturally the original module, so naturality of the
continuity map transports its isomorphism. Every other cohomology object is zero;
the constant-scalar restriction is additive, hence has zero sections there, and the
colimit of the resulting zero diagram is zero. Its continuity map is an isomorphism.
